What drives a restaurant's rating?

Cleaning and exploring 9,551 Zomato restaurants across 15 countries: from a messy raw file to statistically tested findings.

9,551restaurants
15countries
141cities
145cuisines
78%have a rating
3.44mean rating
SummaryCleaningFindingsRecommendationsMethod & caveats

Key takeaways

Four things to know before the charts.

Rating follows popularity and price

Votes (ρ = 0.68) and price tier (3.24 → 3.89) track rating far more than any service feature.

Table booking is a proxy for price

The +0.24 rating gap in India reverses inside the upscale tiers.

Data quality changed the story

Treating 2,148 "0" ratings as missing lifts the mean from 2.67 to 3.44.

Sample bias limits comparisons

India is 91% of rows, so city and country rankings compare samples, not markets.

Findings

Rating analyses use rated restaurants only; service comparisons use India only.

01

The data is a Delhi story

India is 90.6% of all restaurants and Delhi NCR alone is 83%. Outside NCR the file holds only about 20 restaurants per city.

02

Ratings are bell-shaped, centred near 3.4

Mean 3.44. Only 301 restaurants are "Excellent" (4.5+). 22.5% have no rating at all (cleaned from a hidden 0).

03

More votes, higher ratings

Spearman ρ = 0.68. Mean rating rises from 2.98 (≤10 votes) to 4.20 (1,000+ votes). 32% of restaurants have under 10 votes, so many ratings are noisy.

04

Pricier restaurants rate higher

Mean rating climbs from 3.24 (budget) to 3.89 (fine dining), Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.001. In India, cost per person vs rating: ρ = 0.33.

05

Table booking's "rating boost" is mostly a price effect

In India, booking restaurants average 3.55 vs 3.31, but inside the Upscale and Fine-dining tiers they rate lower (3.59 vs 3.79, 3.62 vs 3.94). Online delivery shows no consistent effect (3.37 vs 3.34).

06

Which cuisines win in India

Mediterranean (3.98), European (3.91) and Asian (3.85) rate highest; Mithai (3.14) and Raw Meats (3.07) lowest. North Indian is the most common primary cuisine (2,992).

07

Wider menus, slightly higher ratings

Mean rating goes from 3.40 (one cuisine) to 3.66 (five or more), but the correlation is weak (ρ ≈ 0.12) and cost rises alongside.

08

Cities and localities

Ghaziabad, Faridabad (3.10) and Noida (3.16) rate lowest; London (4.54) and Rio (4.49) highest, though on ~20 restaurants each. Connaught Place is the busiest locality (122 restaurants, avg 3.78).

09

Countries are not comparable like-for-like

India averages 3.35 versus 3.6–4.5 elsewhere, but foreign samples are small and 99–100% rated, so this is not a quality ranking. Online delivery exists only for India (28%) and the UAE (47%).

10

Delhi NCR: dense, with mixed quality

Grey dots are unrated restaurants. Coordinates were validated against country bounds; 500 unusable points were excluded.

11

What moves with rating

Votes 0.68, cost per person 0.45, price range 0.40, table booking 0.13, cuisines 0.12, online delivery −0.04 (Spearman, rated restaurants).

12

Big chains rate below average

Domino's 2.93, Cafe Coffee Day 3.00 and Subway 3.00 sit well under the 3.44 mean; Starbucks (3.81) and Barbeque Nation (4.35) stand out.

Recommendations

Show vote counts next to ratings

32% of restaurants have fewer than 10 votes, and rating rises with votes. A rating from 5 votes should be labelled provisional.

Fix the data capture

Store "not rated" as missing, not 0, fix the currency labels and text encoding, and validate coordinates at entry.

Next: model and deep-dive

Predict rating from cost, votes, cuisines, services and location, and analyse Delhi NCR localities, the only area with enough data.

Method & caveats

Methods: Spearman correlation, Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney tests (ratings are not normally distributed), stratified comparisons by price tier to control for confounding.

Caveats: USD costs use fixed, approximate 2018 exchange rates. About 70 damaged text cells could not be restored. The sample is not random, so results are associations, not causes.
